entry.evidence: the gravimeter showed, unexpectedly, that it can act as an early-warning device, a couple of hours before the extreme event

sequences.source_document: Van Camp et al. 2022, Earth's Future (HAL PDF)

steps.action: Frames extreme floods as a stress on monitoring networks and asks how all available sensors can be combined to track such events.
steps.quote: Extreme disasters also challenge the scientific communities.

steps.action: Cites geodetic and seismic networks as opportunistic hydrological sensors, including Cook et al. (2021) on seismic early warning of flow events.
steps.quote: A seismic network can also act as a valuable early warning system

steps.action: Notes that space techniques lack the resolution for flash floods and states the aim: show that seismic and gravity data can monitor the July 2021 flood and give early warning.
steps.quote: In this study, we show the possibility of using seismic and gravity measurements integrating the whole vadose zone

steps.action: Takes the Bernd storm over the Vesdre watershed as the live event, using cited record rainfall at Jalhay, the return period and peak flows (Zeimetz et al. 2021).
steps.quote: recorded the highest cumulative value ever recorded within 48 hr in Belgium

steps.action: Recalls the authors' earlier characterization of the Membach superconducting gravimeter: about 400 m footprint and an admittance of -0.39 nm s-2 per mm of water.
steps.quote: integrating the soil water in a radius of about 400 m around the instrument

steps.action: Takes as the expectation the proportional gravity response to precipitation established at the station since 2004.
steps.quote: the gravity has always reacted proportionally to precipitation

steps.action: Compares the July 2021 gravity decrease (43 nm/s2) with the previous maximum (41 nm/s2 in July 2014) and with the wet-season baseline, and finds it unprecedented.
steps.quote: which is unprecedented

steps.action: Computes a moving-window spectrum of the vertical broadband seismometer and finds 1-8 Hz noise reaching twice its earlier level during the night of 14-15 July.
steps.quote: the standard deviation of the seismic noise reached twice the level observed before

steps.action: Reads the noise bursts SA-SD as sudden changes in river flow and links SB to the flow that destroyed the station lifeline at 22:31, reconstructing the sequence of events.
steps.quote: there were at least four changes in the noise regime, most probably related to sudden changes in the river flow

steps.action: Matches burst SD (00:15) with an eyewitness report of a roaring and a 'tsunami' at 00:30, 3 km downstream in Béthane.
steps.quote: It coincides with the detailed testimony 3 km downstream in Béthane

steps.action: Places the event's peak flows at Eupen and Verviers against the decade-long flow records to show how exceptional it was.
steps.quote: For the last 10 years, the flow at the Eupen reservoir has never exceeded 56 m³/s

steps.action: Examines the seismic spectra over a week centred on the event as a baseline and finds no comparable signal beyond working-hour and microseismic variations.
steps.quote: we could not evidence any signal similar to the observed one in July 2021

steps.action: Converts gravity to equivalent water height with the -0.39 nm/s2/mm admittance and assembles it with radar-gauge rainfall, the Eupen inflow hydrogram (about 65% of the Vesdre flow) and the seismic spectrum.
steps.quote: inferred from gravity change by using an admittance of

steps.action: Shows that in the first rain episode (A-B, 48 mm) the gravimeter gave a similar water height (40 mm), as the established regularity predicts for unsaturated soil.
steps.quote: the gravimeter provided a similar water equivalent height (40 mm)

steps.action: Interprets the shrinking gravity response during the 14 July rain (episode D) as progressive saturation of the weathered zone.
steps.quote: the gravimeter evidenced a rising saturation of the weathered zone above

steps.action: Shows that when rain re-intensified after 18 h (E), gravity stayed stable while inflow to the Eupen reservoir rose much faster than before, to 232 m³/s (F).
steps.quote: Simultaneously, gravity remained essentially stable.

steps.action: Retains the claim that the gravimeter detected the saturation of the subsoil and soil in real time within about 400 m of the instrument.
steps.quote: a gravimeter was able to detect in real-time the saturation of the subsoil and soil

steps.action: Extends the claim from the gravimeter footprint to the plateau of most intense rain, assuming similar hydrogeology, and proposes that the gravimeter marked the saturation limit before the flood.
steps.quote: It is reasonable to assume that the gravimeter may have indicated the saturation limit

steps.action: Concludes that continuous gravity monitoring could improve early warning, allowing a warning a few hours before the flow increase.
steps.quote: we demonstrated that continuous gravity monitoring could improve early warning systems

steps.action: Poses future work: gravimeter arrays for soil saturation, and a local seismic network with river monitoring to interpret the noise spectrum.
steps.quote: which will require the installation of a local seismic network and monitoring of the river

tree.answer: Yes: a strong flood signature in the gravity and seismic records at Membach
Partly: saturation is inferred from gravity-derived water height, not measured directly
Show that gravity and seismic data monitor the flood and could give early warning
No stated rivals; the turbulence and bed-load reading of the seismic spectrum is deferred as speculative
None derived; only a contrast with the proportional-response expectation
Found: a live extreme storm and flood recorded by a permanent station

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: No repetition; one event, compared only with the July 2014 maximum
Limited checks: a week-long seismic baseline, an eyewitness timing match and the expected first-episode gravity response
Kept: the gravimeter detected subsoil saturation in real time
Two anonymous reviewers are acknowledged; no review file was supplied

end.claim: During the July 2021 flood, the Membach superconducting gravimeter detected in real time the saturation of the subsoil and soil around it, after which renewed rain produced a sharp runoff increase, so real-time gravity could support flash-flood early warning.

decisive_move.sentence: Setting the stable gravity signal against the accelerated reservoir inflow after the rain re-intensified (episodes E-F) is what turns the gravity plateau into evidence of saturation.

gates.evidence: The data come from a permanent station recording an unplanned event, so no hypothesis directed acquisition (p. 2). The saturation reading could have failed had gravity kept tracking rainfall while inflow surged, but no rival or formal test is stated (p. 5). Nothing was fixed in advance: no saturation threshold or warning rule was set before the event; the early-warning claim is retrospective.

imports.item: newspaper eyewitness testimony of the flood timing at Béthane (Vincent 2021)
absolute quantum gravimeters proposed for future gravity imagers
low-cost MEMS relative gravimeters proposed for arrays

novelty_claims.quote: This shows, for the first time to our knowledge, how a gravimeter was able to detect in real-time the saturation of the subsoil and soil
provide, together, a new early warning system, informing about the flash flooding hazard several hours in advance

limits: This is a commentary on a single event; no regularity across events is fitted, and the only historical comparison is the July 2014 gravity maximum. Sub-claims: the seismic reconstruction of the flood sequence is a best_explanation, supported only by an eyewitness timing match and a one-week baseline; the authors call a physical interpretation speculative. The extension from the 400 m gravimeter footprint to the rain-hit plateau is an assumption (best_explanation at most). The early-warning capability is not characterized: no lead time, threshold, false-alarm rate or frozen forecast is given (status none; it is asserted retrospectively). The paper does not say whether the -0.39 nm/s2/mm admittance holds under saturated conditions, does not model hydrology to test the saturation interpretation, and uses the Eupen inflow as a proxy for the Vesdre flow (about 65%). Inference: the analysis seems to have been chosen after the event was seen. No review file was supplied, so the review history is unknown beyond the acknowledgment of two anonymous reviewers.

disagreements.target: space gravimetry and microwave soil-moisture remote sensing as flood-monitoring tools
disagreements.support: The paper cites the time and space resolution of these products, and the shallow depth sensed by microwave methods, as too coarse for local flash floods, unlike ground geophysical networks.
disagreements.quote: it is not yet possible to use space gravimetry to investigate local flash floods

disagreements.target: physical seismic-noise models of turbulence and bed load (Burtin et al. 2011; Gimbert et al. 2014) applied to this record
disagreements.support: The paper states that without a local seismic network and river monitoring, such an interpretation of the Membach spectrum would be speculative.
disagreements.quote: would be speculative without a comprehensive investigation, including a local seismic network

alternatives_considered.chosen: qualitative timing reconstruction of noise bursts as flow changes
alternatives_considered.alternatives: interpreting the seismic spectrum in terms of water turbulence and bed load (Burtin et al. 2011; Gimbert et al. 2014)
alternatives_considered.reason: speculative without a local seismic network and appropriate river monitoring

alternatives_considered.chosen: Eupen dam inflow hydrogram (reconstructed from reservoir level and discharge)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: downstream limnimetric gauges such as the Verviers flow meter
alternatives_considered.reason: only complete hydrogram available upstream of the station; the downstream network was damaged or destroyed

alternatives_considered.alternatives: space gravimetry and microwave remote sensing of soil moisture
alternatives_considered.reason: insufficient time and space resolution, and shallow sensing depth, of space techniques
